clue.text: Run into English poet, shy type without a partner

indicators.note: into says the word for run is pushed inside the poet's name

parts.note: Edmund Waller was a seventeenth-century English poet
to run, as water does, is to flow

explanation.surface: A dancer who bumps into a poet is a shy type left standing alone at the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run into' looks like a phrasal verb meaning collide; 'into' is the container signal. The poet is the seventeenth-century Edmund Waller, little read today.
explanation.definitionFit: At a dance, a girl left sitting by the wall with no partner is the classic idiom for a shy person.

clue.text: Certify such an officer?

definitions.meaning: a rank in the armed forces between commissioned and non-commissioned officers

explanation.walkthrough: A warrant officer holds rank by warrant rather than commission.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something, and the rank of a forces officer appointed by such a document.

clue.text: .Servant's dismal day off

indicators.note: off says these letters have gone bad and come out in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A domestic servant is having a miserable day off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'day off' looks like a holiday; 'off' is the anagram signal, rearranging DISMAL DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A female attendant to a noblewoman is a kind of domestic servant.

clue.text: Wind instrument kept under the stairs in black box

indicators.note: in a down clue the instrument kept under sits below the stairs

parts.note: a flight is a run of stairs
the recorder is a woodwind instrument played in schools

explanation.surface: A flute or pipe is stored in the black box in the cupboard under the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black box' sounds like a storage case but is the aircraft's data recorder.
explanation.definitionFit: The so-called black box on an aircraft logs data and cockpit voices for crash investigators.

clue.text: Guy not allowed initially to remain longer

indicators.note: initially puts the word for not allowed at the start, ahead of the guy

parts.note: a ball or batsman ruled not allowed is out
a guy is a rope used as a stay

explanation.surface: A man refused entry still hangs around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is a guy rope, a STAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain past the time one is welcome or expected.

clue.text: Hopes to be about to have baby son

parts.note: a pregnant woman is said to be expecting
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Parents look forward to the birth of a baby boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope for something is to look forward to it confidently.

clue.text: Circus performer's escape reported

indicators.note: reported means the clue's word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to escape is to flee

explanation.surface: A circus act makes a getaway, and the newspapers carry the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The flea circus is a novelty sideshow in which tiny insects supposedly pull carts and perform tricks.

clue.text: Start of long account journalist spiked

indicators.note: Start of picks only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor kills the opening of a long report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiked' looks like a newsroom term for an article dropped; it means a drink laced with alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink secretly fortified with alcohol or a drug is said to be laced.

clue.text: Developments in USSR are encouraging one

indicators.note: developments in says these letters change shape into something new

explanation.surface: Changes in the Soviet Union are promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developments in' rearranges USSR ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reassures or gives confidence to another is this kind of person.

clue.text: A warning to people, i.e. don't change what's already said

parts.note: taken as written
golfers shout fore to warn people of a flying ball
men can mean people

indicators.note: don't change looks like advice; change is the instruction to rearrange those letters

explanation.surface: A warning that people must not alter a statement once it has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges I.E. DON'T into TIONED; 'don't change' reads as a command to leave things as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase refers to something mentioned earlier in a text or talk.

clue.text: Lines in circle, each about a cubit in length

definitions.meaning: straight lines from the centre of a circle to its edge

definitions.text: each about a cubit in length
definitions.meaning: the forearm bones bearing this plural name are roughly the length of a cubit, an old measure based on the forearm

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about lines in a circle, measured in an ancient unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition switches from geometry to anatomy: the cubit was the length from elbow to fingertip, and that forearm bone shares its name with the circle's line.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the geometric line from centre to circumference is also the plural of a forearm bone.

clue.text: They can make a good impression with kind looks

definitions.text: They can make a good impression

parts.note: a kind or sort is a type
looks, as in expressions, are faces

explanation.surface: People with kindly looks tend to make a good impression on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' sounds social, but it is the printer's impression made by a set of characters on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fonts in printing are what physically press their letter shapes onto the page.

clue.text: The Eastern act is unusually artistic

indicators.note: unusually says these letters are set out in an unusual new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatrical performance from the East is remarkably artistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges THE, E (Eastern), ACT and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concerned with beauty and taste in art is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Haggard condition?

definitions.meaning: The clue gives his surname for his first name
a clause added to a contract or bill as a proviso

explanation.surface: Asking what condition leaves a person looking haggard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' with its capital hidden at the start of the clue looks like the adjective for gaunt; it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's forename is also a word for an extra clause or proviso attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Cupbearer given time to dine on fish

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another places it before what follows

parts.note: to dine is to eat
the ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: A royal cupbearer is allowed time to sit down to a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cupbearer' suggests a royal servant, but it is a flat tray for carrying teacups.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray used to carry cups of tea literally bears cups.

clue.text: Remains assembled for conference of specialists

indicators.note: assembled says the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bones or relics are gathered for a meeting of experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges REMAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting for discussion among experts or students is the usual sense of this word.

clue.text: Expert who can provide the latest word

definitions.text: Expert who can provide the latest word

parts.words: Expert who can provide the latest word
parts.note: the latest word is a newly coined term, not the latest news

explanation.walkthrough: 'the latest word' sounds like news; it means a brand-new word, coined by a specialist in such coinages.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who coins or studies newly invented words.

clue.text: Where passenger's left to get a drink

definitions.meaning: the passenger compartment attached to the left of a British motorcycle
a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice

explanation.surface: A traveller is dropped off somewhere to grab a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorcycles carry the passenger pod on the left-hand side, since traffic drives on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both the passenger pod beside a motorbike and a brandy cocktail.

clue.text: FBI agents in co-ordinated group taking part

indicators.note: in says the agents are placed inside the group

parts.note: a matching set is a co-ordinated group
G-men were the US government agents of the FBI

explanation.surface: Federal agents join a group to take part in an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men, short for government men, was the 1930s American nickname for FBI agents; 'taking' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or section of a whole.

clue.text: Service char, for example, with a poor reputation

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: A forces cleaning lady with a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like a British charwoman or cleaner; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish, disreputable and unconventional in a slightly dashing way.

clue.text: Like mushrooms and game I put in stock

indicators.note: put in says the game and I are placed inside the word for stock

parts.note: a stock or reserve of money is a fund
go is the Japanese board game
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tosses mushrooms and game into a stockpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks culinary beside mushrooms and game, but it is FUND, holding GO and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means resembling a fungus, the group that includes mushrooms.

clue.text: Refrain appropriate to Pooh

parts.note: something appropriate to a person is for them
Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: A song chorus suited to Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a song's chorus; it is the verb to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back from doing something.

clue.text: Blow up gun dealt with outside

indicators.note: outside says the words for dealt with go round the gun

parts.note: to have done a job is to have dealt with it
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A gun is handled outside before it explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' suggests an explosion beside 'gun'; it means swell or inflate.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell or inflate by pressure from within.

clue.text: The Italian rejected by wicked princess is a hopeless fellow

indicators.note: rejected by says the Italian article is dropped from the princess's name

parts.note: Goneril is King Lear's cruel elder daughter in Shakespeare
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian suitor spurned by a wicked princess is a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected by' removes IL (Italian 'the') from GONERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond help or certain to die or fail is colloquially called this.

clue.text: Part of fine palace where a king rules

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a grand palace is where the king holds court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan state was a kingdom ruled by a monarch until 2008.

clue.text: Implements useful for attending to hot dogs

definitions.text: Implements useful for attending to hot dogs

parts.words: Implements useful for attending to hot dogs
parts.note: the hot dogs are firedogs, the metal stands holding logs in a hearth, tended with poker and tongs

explanation.surface: Kitchen tools for serving sausages in buns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dogs' suggests sausages; firedogs (andirons) are the hearth supports, and the poker, tongs and shovel tend them.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker, tongs and shovel kept beside a hearth for tending the burning logs on their supports.

clue.text: You may well see stars if this fails to get into print

definitions.text: You may well see stars if this fails to get into print

parts.words: You may well see stars if this fails to get into print
parts.note: a swear word too rude to print is replaced by asterisks, the stars

explanation.surface: Being knocked out and seeing stars when a story fails to be published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see stars' suggests a blow to the head; newspapers print an oath as a row of asterisks.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath or swear word, which a newspaper censors with asterisks.

clue.text: Sound from electric current in hooter

indicators.note: in says the current's symbol sits inside the word for hooter

parts.note: hooter is British slang for the nose
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A car horn sounds when electric current runs through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' looks like a horn, which fits 'Sound'; it is slang for NOSE, holding I.
explanation.definitionFit: Any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one, is called this.

clue.text: Inclination to attack with weapon

definitions.meaning: a slope or lean, as of a table off level
to charge at with a lance in a joust

explanation.surface: A tendency to lash out with arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Knights in a joust 'tilt at' each other with lances, which gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean or slope, and a jousting charge with a lance, share this one word.

clue.text: Crumbling old hat, not expected-to last long

parts.note: short pastry is crumbly, so short means crumbling
old hat means out of date or dated

explanation.surface: A battered old hat that is not likely to survive much longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' looks like an anagram signal for 'old hat'; but HAT has no place in the answer. It is SHORT, as in short pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or a bill with an early expiry date is not meant to last long.
